case_name: Inference API Abuse -> Model Extraction and Training-Data Probing
scenario_type: High-Volume Systematic Querying of a Public ML Inference Endpoint
source: Newly authored for securebert-aia-correlation demo corpus
investigation_objective: Determine whether unusual query patterns against the company's public fraud-scoring inference API reflect a legitimate integration partner, a misconfigured internal job, or an attacker attempting to extract/clone the proprietary model and probe for memorized training data.

likely_adversary_objective.summary: Reconstruct a functional clone of a proprietary ML model through systematic API querying, and probe for leakage of memorized training data, without ever touching the hosting infrastructure directly.
likely_adversary_objective.attack_style: Black-box model extraction / membership inference via public inference API

alerts.title: Anomalous Query Volume from Single API Key
alerts.description: A single API key issued a query volume 40x above its historical peak within a 2-hour window.
evidence: Queries: 186,400 in 2 hours vs. 90-day peak of 4,100/day
Key was provisioned for a low-volume sandbox integration
Requests originated from a narrow IP range not matching the partner's registered egress
No corresponding support/integration ticket for a volume increase
alerts.why_it_matters: A 40x volume spike on a sandbox key with no change request is the first sign of automated, non-organic querying.

alerts.title: Systematic Input-Space Sweep Pattern Detected
alerts.description: Query inputs followed a dense, systematic sweep across the model's feature space rather than resembling organic transaction data.
evidence: Feature vectors show near-uniform grid coverage across 6 input dimensions
Real transaction traffic does not exhibit this distribution
Query diversity metric is 97th percentile vs. a near-zero baseline for legitimate partners
Pattern consistent with surrogate-model training data generation
alerts.why_it_matters: This querying pattern is consistent with an attacker systematically sampling a model's decision boundary to train a surrogate (cloned) model that mimics its behavior.

alerts.title: High-Confidence-Score Query Clustering Near Decision Boundary
alerts.description: A disproportionate share of queries cluster near the model's decision threshold rather than reflecting the real-world class distribution.
evidence: 38% of queries scored within +/-0.03 of the decision threshold
Production transaction traffic shows under 2% of queries in this band
Boundary-focused sampling is a recognized technique for refining a cloned model's decision surface
alerts.why_it_matters: Legitimate transaction traffic does not cluster around a model's decision boundary; an attacker refining a clone does.

alerts.title: Repeated Near-Duplicate Queries With Single-Field Perturbation
alerts.description: Many queries differ from a prior query by exactly one perturbed field, consistent with sensitivity probing of individual features.
evidence: 1,240 query pairs differ by a single field value
Perturbation step sizes are uniform and systematic, not representative of organic transactions
Pattern matches known feature-sensitivity probing methodology
alerts.why_it_matters: Systematic single-field perturbation is a textbook step in reverse-engineering a model's feature sensitivities.

alerts.title: Queries Resembling Known Training-Set Record Shapes
alerts.source: ML Inference Monitoring / Data Science Team
alerts.description: A subset of query inputs closely match the statistical shape of records known to exist in the model's original training set, consistent with a membership-inference probe for training-data leakage.
evidence: 212 queries match training-record statistical fingerprints at over 90% similarity
Legitimate partner traffic has no access to or knowledge of training data composition
Membership-inference probing can reveal whether specific records were used in training, a data-privacy exposure
alerts.why_it_matters: This goes beyond cloning model behavior and probes whether specific real records were memorized -- a direct privacy exposure.

alerts.title: Partner Integration Key Used Outside Registered IP Range
alerts.description: The sandbox API key was used from IP ranges not matching the partner's registered egress addresses on file.
evidence: Registered egress: single /28 block in us-east
Observed source: distributed across 14 IPs in 3 different cloud provider ranges
No IP allowlist change request on file
alerts.why_it_matters: A legitimately-issued key used from unregistered, distributed infrastructure suggests the key itself was repurposed by someone other than the partner.

alerts.title: Billing/Cost Anomaly on Inference Compute
alerts.description: Inference compute costs attributable to this API key spiked sharply, consistent with sustained high-volume querying.
evidence: Inference compute cost 23x daily average attributable to this key
Cost spike time-aligned with the query-volume anomaly
No corresponding increase in legitimate transaction volume from the partner
alerts.why_it_matters: Beyond IP theft risk, sustained extraction-style querying against a paid inference endpoint also creates a direct, measurable cost impact.

threat_context.threat_summary: No system was breached and no credential was stolen. A single low-volume sandbox API key was used to run a systematic, high-density sweep against the production fraud-scoring inference endpoint consistent with black-box model extraction and membership-inference probing of the training set -- the entire attack surface here is the model's own public prediction interface.

observed_evidence: Abused a legitimately-issued but narrowly-scoped sandbox API key from unregistered IP ranges
Scripted querying conducted entirely over ordinary HTTPS API calls, indistinguishable at the network layer from normal partner traffic
186,400 queries in 2 hours via a public inference endpoint
Query patterns consistent with training-data membership-inference probing

mitre_atlas_mapping.technique_name: Exfiltration via AI Inference API: Extract AI Model
observed_evidence: Systematic feature-space sweep and decision-boundary clustering consistent with surrogate model extraction

detection_recommendation.detection_goal: Detect model-extraction-style querying against a public inference API by combining volume anomaly, input-space sweep patterns, and decision-boundary clustering.

sigma_rule.title: ML Inference API Model Extraction Pattern

tuning_recommendations: Baseline per-key query volume and input diversity individually -- a fixed global threshold misses low-and-slow extraction attempts.
Flag decision-boundary clustering and single-field perturbation sweeps even at moderate volume; these are stronger extraction signals than raw request count alone.
